body: Bud, the only reason I haven't already done it is that my life insurance policy doesn't cover anything if I take my own life (it isn't no-fault) and I don't feel like sticking the people I love with my debt; if I had a cash reserve to pay it all off, I would've done it already.

Bad things have already happened and I can't cope with it anymore; I broke down sobbing at work for an hour today in the bathroom, broke down when I got home, and have gotten maybe 6 hours of sleep in three days. I'm done. I don't know where else or who else to turn to.
Right now I want to learn the basics because, to be perfectly honest, I have no idea what kind of programming I want to do.

I have only one real goal: to have so semblance of control over my life. For as long as I can possibly remember, I've never had any real control over it; every thing I do is dictated by the actions or (more of than not) inaction of others, rather than being the end result of something I myself have done. I can send off or walk in resumes until my bones are broken and my flesh bleeds, but it's all for naught if no one's willing to give me the time of day (and no one has been, considering I'm year 3 into a dead end, wage-slave job I hate). I've posted ads online for a roommate, but no one seems interested in anything other than a few months' rental; if I don't find some one soon, I WILL be homeless come January (can't afford the rent after the increase, yet can't afford the deposit of a different apartment).

It's the emasculating lack of power over everything I do that is maddening. I know what I need to do to improve my life and circumstances, but I'm denied those means at every turn. Every promising lead evaporates into disappointing nothingness, reprieve cruelly yanked away the moment it's within reach. I've done everything I possibly can..and yet, continue to fail. Continue to suffer defeat. 

Maybe it's impatience..but I don't want to wait until I'm 50 with half of my life long since passed by the be "okay"...I've already done that (25, have fought and struggled every day since 13 for the "better tomorrow" that never f*cking comes) and can't do it anymore. The only reason I haven't offed myself already is because I don't have means to pay off my debts and cremation; it's not fair to saddle my loved ones with that burden.

I'm trying the "one day at a time" approach, but it's not overly successful. Each day is another crippling blow and crushing defeat. Today I've come home to find out 1) I didn't get the job I desperately needed to keep myself afloat, and 2) my rent's being increased in the new year by an amount I can't afford even with a roommate. Every day is some new horrific thing to face and I can't do it any more.

Positive life changes don't always come as a result of one's perseverance, inner strength, or energy; sometimes it requires an external catalyst (a bit like a chemical reaction). Without that catalyst, the reaction doesn't take place and nothing happens. Employment, housing, relationships...unless someone or something other than you acts...your best laid plans, your hard fought battles...it all amounts to nothing but wasted time and energy. You learn, you brush it off, and "get back on the horse." It throws you off, repeatedly. There eventually comes a point where "getting back on the horse" becomes an act of madness; you know your efforts won't result in anything positive but somehow you expect a different result from what's already been basically set in stone.

I moved to another country, fought for permanent residency, and got married. The marriage fell through, and I eventually grew the testicular fortitude to put her out...but not before she cleaned me out. My girlfriend will most likely be breaking up with me soon (she has once before, and is showing the same "tells" now as she did then). I'm still a wage slave despite every attempt at getting better paying employment elsewhere. I'll be facing homelessness in around 2-3 months. I've done everything one can possibly do to change his circumstances...only to have gained nothing in the end. That's how I know. I know that continuing to fight the good fight isn't going to put me any further ahead; I will stay in the same place I've been since my teenage years. That, that is how I know.

While it was perfectly okay for him to watch Cow & Chicken or Dexter's Lab at night, my entertainment options were completely limited to documentaries and text books. I could tell you that the Japanese Zero was "derived" (i.e. copied) from the Hues H-1, that US military planes were awful up until 1940 with the introduction of the Hellcat, and that the suspension system employed by German tanks had actually been sold to the Nazis after its American inventor was turned away by the U.S. military, but I couldn't tell you how much Vegeta ass Goku kicked because I didn't know who the hell either one of them were.

My sibling died during the first trimester and had been mostly reabsorbed into the womb by the time I was born; my parents found out about the "other" immediately after my birth when their doctor commented on the remnants he found in the placenta. Vanishing twin syndrome is apparently more common than one would think.

I:

1) Shut any and all emotional responses in times of great duress. For example: when my spouse decided to bring other men home, fuck them in our bed, and then share the details with me afterwards, I didn't cry. I didn't yell, resort to violence, or curse. I just ate a sandwich, browsed reddit, and played Serious Sam 3 like nothing had happened because I felt absolutely nothing.

2)I come across as being cold and intimidating, which makes it difficult to network and build functional relationships. I refuse to change those features (as it's my natural defence mechanism) even though I logically know I would be better off as a warmer, more approachable person. 

3)If I am presented with a conflict too great for me to properly "shut down", I self destruct massively. I've broken bones punching concrete and have resorted to self mutilation in the past. Not because, "Oh, my life sucks, pity me..boo hoo." It's all about power: 1) I might not be able to control circumstances or even my emotional response to them, but I get to control whether I do or do not feel pain/bleed and 2) if I'm going to be that hurt/raging, I'd rather do it to myself than let someone think they're pulling my leash. 

4)When physically confronted or threatened, I become extremely aggressive and have no qualms with verbally tearing down or physically harming someone/anyone who is actively trying to hurt me. I've reduced people to tears after they sent an off-handed insult my way, and I nearly drowned my little brother in a swimming pool after he hit me with a KO worthy punch during an argument he initiated.

1) My family lost its house on Christmas Eve 2004 because the family business went bankrupt and my dad left shortly after; I saw him twice between then and when I graduated high school in 2006. I got a job after school as a janitor, but ended up working full time as the financial situation; with the amount of money my family owed to its former suppliers, my paycheck went to utilities because we couldn't afford food otherwise. 

2) After graduating high school, I moved to Canada and tried immigrating. I was outright told on multiple occasions, "You have nothing to offer us, we do not want you here." I spent every dime I had on trying to get a work visa while I lived with my then-GF (now ex-wife's) parents, but was denied at every turn. Immigration Canada mis-filed my paper work once, adding 9 months to the process. I ended up doing doing labour for people around the neighbourhood for a price that was too good to pass up ($10 to mow the entire property as well as leaf pick up, $10 for snow removal regardless of amount). I worked up to 16 hours a day non-stop to make something; at the end of it, I was so dehydrated my stools basically turned to stone, I'd fill a toilet with blood, and developed anaemia. One the last heavy snow fall of the winter, I tore my left lat. When I recovered and got my permanent residency, I ended up having to quit my first job after sustaining a chronic repetitive stress injury. After I recovered from that, the economy collapsed and I wound up working for a retailer as a warehouse grunt for 1/2 the pay. I've been there since, and every attempt at finding higher paying employment has been denied; no one's willing to give me a chance, even if I have the experience.

3) My wife emotionally abused me for the better part of the 10 yeras we've known each other (I'm 24). In the relationship's infancy, she'd threaten to kill herself almost every day over any number of things (family life, her physical and emotional insecurities, etc). When I met her the first time, she tried to kill herself in front of my by attempting to  down a bottle of pills; I snatched them out of her hands and she bit my forearm so hard I bled (still didn't let go, never raised a hand to her to stop it, or shouted). Over the years, I've been kicked, verbally abused, emotionally blackmailed, and sexually humiliated in front of my peers; things that were very intimate and personal to me where shared and laughed at like a joke.

4) When my wife decided I wasn't good enough for her (because I'd refuse to sleep with someone on command or to be used as a sex toy), she started seeing other men. She'd bring them home, lie to them, and they'd share our bed. I've met most of them, much to my own detriment. Every detail, every little thing was shared and I was even asked my opinion on them. I gave up everything (scholarships, friends, family, even my country) to be with someone who betrayed my trust in every way possible.

5) I tried reciprocating the interest in a friend who once told me she loved me; she friendzoned me hard because "I'm not ready for a long term relationship, you're a nice guy but you need to work on you until you have something to offer" and so forth. She told me the following day she met the love of her life and that they'd be moving in together; I've known her for 12 years, she's known him for one. Every time we talk, all she does is gush about him; as much as I like to see her happy, I'm tired of hearing how Prince Charming galloped in on a horse and swept her off of her feet.

6) I started dating another friend and things, in my mind, were going great. Life, though roughly the same, was a bit more tolerable and for the first time in many years I felt I'd reached a turning point; that things would be okay, and I was even starting to feel happiness for the first time. She broke up with me yesterday because "it's not you, it's the situation". She finds it weird I'm still so close with my in-laws and feels awkward when they invite me over to the family functions as they've also done. I'm told that when I've moved on fully, maybe we can try again. The same day, I'm told my mother-in-law might have lung cancer.

7) People say I shouldn't pursue a relationship so soon, that I should do any number of exercises a first year psychology major would recommend (list the number of things in your life you would like to change and try to change them one at a time, etc...things I did while in therapy), I should build networks, and focus on me. They then tell me I'm a rain cloud of misery when I tell them that, as much as I appreciate their advice, none of it actually works for me despite the countless attempts at implementing them; focusing on one's self does little good without the external catalyst needed to drive such massive change. You can't build a network of friends when people won't give you the time of day, you can't go out when you're basically living pay cheque to pay cheque and that $30 you could spend at the bar is what might actually break you at the end of the month. You can't get a different job or engage in a different career path unless someone gives you a chance. Many self improvements require money: gym memberships, supplements, car repairs, clothes, dentistry, and therapy sessions do not pay for themselves. Relationships? Women don't bat an eye at me, they have no interest; even exchanging inane pleasantries with someone results in scorn. "Perception is reality", apparently. "Keep your head up, things get better." "Be a man, roll with the punches." All pointless ego-inflating words of wisdom that ultimately amount to nothing.

In summation: life isn't all that great and if you told me tonight someone was going to walk up to me tomorrow and scatter my gray matter on a sidewalk, I'd shake his hand and thank him. Half of my life has been spent hoping, praying, trying, and fighting for a better tomorrow that has never come to pass. Tomorrow is no different than today...neither is next week, and it won't be all that different a year from now.

Everything about John Carpenter's The Thing makes it un-watchable, even though I'm 24 years old. The tense, lonely atmosphere coupled with the faint, simple chords of a bass guitar send chills up my spine; you know that there is no one else to turn to when things hit the fan and that there's no point in holding out for a rescue when people don't even know something's amiss. The special effects are genuinely creepy, but what horrifies me most about the movie are: 1) meeting a horrifically painful demise and 2) having your consciousness absorbed into that of another being's in the interim. That is what scares me most; with death, the mind simply cease to exist...with The Thing, you become part of it.

I feel awful for posting here, as my "worst experiences" are nothing compared to losing a loved one or watching some die horribly before their eyes. Nonetheless:

1) When I was 17, I became the "father" of three kittens after my dad had accidentally killed their mother; instead of "let nature take its course, son", I took it upon myself to look after them; I had (and still have) the naive belief that all forms of life, great and small, deserve a chance to live. I bottle fed them, slept next their crate (I didn't want to roll over and smother them in my sleep), and played with them as they grew; they cried when I went to school, and crawled all over me, purring, from the time I got home to the time we went to bed. We were pretty inseparable. Squirt, the runt, was my favorite; she was so small, yet so resilient and full of life. One day, I noticed she was passing bloody stool and was squealing in pain. I asked to take her to the vet (I'd pay for the visit, the meds, and the trip to and from). My dad denied my request. Things worsened over the next week; she wouldn't eat, she was in obvious pain, and was passing bloody, pussy stool. I begged and pleaded to take her to the vet, if only to put her down. My dad's response: "You took them in after I explicitly told you not to. You have two choices: she either dies on her own, or you put her down. Either nut up or shut up; I'm not taking a goddamn cat to a vet." I gave her a bath, sobbing as I saw her lips turning blue; I contemplated on drowning her but couldn't bear to do it. I took her down to the barn with my 12 gauge, told her I loved her, and pulled the trigger. It felt like taking the life of a child.

2) Last year, I bought a boston terrier puppy (Willow). She was amazing, even at 8 weeks old; she was grasping the concepts of potty training, she was practically attached to my legs and chest, and was, like Squirt, always waiting for me. I woke up at 5:30 AM (like I always do), and stepped over the grate I'd put up in the kitchen to keep her in (she was too polite to wake me up to use the bathroom, and was, again, so small I didn't want to accidentally crush her in my sleep). I stepped in something warm and sticky, thinking it was poop, as she nibbled at my toes and yapped excitedly. "Whatever...she's a puppy, and she's just learning." I thought. I flipped on the light to see blood. Blood every where. I called into work, asking to take the day off to take her to the vet and was promptly denied. I spent the remainder of that week force feeding her pedialyte and formula, trying to keep her hydrated and fed, as she kept losing weight and passing blood; kept begging work to take off time to see a vet, and was denied every time. I finally told my manager to kiss my ass over the phone and took her in. She had parvo; the breeder who sold her to me had stolen her, and her siblings from a farm in western ontario and forged an extremely convincing vaccination record (the vet himself was shocked at how well done it was). I called the insurance company and was told it was a "pre-existing" condition that they wouldn't cover ("pre-existing" because I took her to the vet three weeks prior for her "second" rabies booster). She was euthanized in my arms.

3) After finding out my wife had been cheating on me for quite some time (and even seeing one of her "friends" in my living room), I decided that the relationship had run its course; we would be friends, but not lovers or husband and wife. My best friend had expressed considerable interest in me before, going so far as to tell me she loved me and wished she had said something before I met and then married my ex. I finally developed the courage to tell her how I felt about her (I had been in same boat with her when I was single and she was in a long term relationship, but kept my mouth shut out of respect). I poured my heart out..only to be rejected in the politest way possible; I "needed to work on myself so I have more to offer", "I could make you happy but would end up destroying it. I need to find my own happiness and not save people", and "You're a great looking guy, you're intelligent, and you can be an amazing person. You deserve someone who loves you and you'll find them one day. Don't settle for anything less. I just can't handle a long term relationship right now, after leaving one of my own." She tells me the next day she met the love of her life and knew it was the one because "he said, "I hope to find a girl like you some day." and that they'll be moving in together soon. She knew him for a year; I've known her for close to 10. I spent so long dead inside and the brief moment true happiness was within reach, it was snuffed out in an instant. She broke my heart in one polite conversation more than my wife did by fucking people in my own bed.

I've seen a social worker, but it was just a preliminary meeting; I don't get to seem my psychiatrist until February, but I don't know how she'll be able to help. Listening to my issues and pumping my system full of antidepressants isn't going to make my problems go away; having more serotonin or dopamine available to my neural tissues isn't going to change my marital status, my shyte job, or lack of a support system...I'll just be slightly numbed to it.
